questions.question: Which of the following best describes the main objective of the financial statements prepared by an organization?

options.A: To provide information about historical sales only.
options.B: To present a true and fair view of the entity’s financial position and performance.
options.C: To guarantee future profitability.
options.D: To serve as legal documents for tax purposes.

questions.explanation: IFRS and GAAP state that the primary purpose of financial statements is to give users a true and fair view of the entity’s financial condition and performance.

questions.question: In a cash basis accounting system, revenues are recognized when:

options.A: When the goods or services are delivered to the customer.
options.B: When cash is received.
options.C: When the invoice is issued.
options.D: At the end of the fiscal year.

questions.explanation: Cash basis accounting records revenue only when cash actually changes hands.

questions.question: A company acquires a machine for $50,000 and estimates its useful life at 8 years. Using the straight‑line depreciation method, what is the annual depreciation expense?

options.A: $6,250 per year
options.B: $5,000 per year
options.C: $7,500 per year
options.D: $12,500 per year

questions.explanation: Straight‑line depreciation equals cost divided by useful life: $50,000 ÷ 8 = $6,250 per year.

questions.question: Depreciation is a non‑cash expense that affects net income. How does it influence net income?

options.A: It increases net income because it raises taxable income.
options.B: It decreases net income because it increases expenses.
options.C: It has no effect on net income.
options.D: It always improves profit margins.

questions.explanation: By reducing reported profits through higher expenses, depreciation lowers net income.

questions.question: Internal controls help prevent errors and fraud. Which of the following is a key component of internal control?

options.A: Regular reconciliation of bank statements.
options.B: Mandatory vacation policy for employees.
options.C: Use of electronic ledgers.
options.D: All of the above.

questions.explanation: Bank statement reconciliations ensure that the accounting records match external evidence, a fundamental control activity.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes photosynthesis in plants?

options.A: The process by which plants produce food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide
options.B: The process of water uptake through the roots
options.C: The process of respiration releasing energy
options.D: The process of decomposition of organic matter

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the synthesis of food (glucose) using light energy, water, and CO₂.

questions.question: Why is soil pH important for crop production?

options.A: It determines the availability of nutrients to plants
options.B: It influences the colour of plant leaves only
options.C: It affects the size of seeds produced
options.D: It controls the rate of photosynthesis directly

questions.explanation: Soil pH affects nutrient solubility and uptake, influencing crop growth.

questions.question: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) primarily involves:

options.A: Using only chemical pesticides to kill pests
options.B: Combining biological, cultural, and chemical methods to control pests while minimising environmental impact
options.C: Planting monocultures to reduce pest diversity
options.D: Ignoring pest population thresholds and treating all infestations equally

questions.explanation: IPM integrates multiple strategies for sustainable pest control.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of legumes?

options.A: They have symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacteria in root nodules
options.B: They grow exclusively in waterlogged soils
options.C: They are primary cereal crops
options.D: They do not form any symbiotic relationships with microbes

questions.explanation: Legumes host Rhizobium bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of mulching in agriculture?

options.A: To increase soil erosion
options.B: To retain soil moisture and regulate soil temperature
options.C: To reduce the amount of organic matter in the soil
options.D: To attract pests and diseases

questions.explanation: Mulch conserves moisture, moderates temperature, and suppresses weeds.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Arabic word مُؤْمِنٌ

options.A: a writer
options.B: a believer
options.C: a teacher
options.D: a farmer

questions.explanation: The word "مُؤْمِنٌ" means "believer" in Arabic, referring to one who believes in God.

questions.question: In the nominal sentence "الْبَيْتُ مَكْتُوبٌ", what is the grammatical case (i'rab) of the word "مَكْتُوبٌ"

options.A: مرفوع
options.B: منصوب
options.C: مجرور
options.D: مست

questions.explanation: "مَكْتُوبٌ" is the predicate of a nominal sentence, so it is in the nominative case (marfu'), matching the subject.

questions.question: Which diacritic marks the short vowel 'u' (damma) on a letter
questions.explanation: The diacritic "ُ" is called damma and represents the short vowel 'u'.

questions.question: Select the correct English translation of the Arabic phrase "إنّ الله مع الصابرين"

options.A: God is with the patient
options.B: God is with the rich
options.C: God is with the brave
options.D: God is with the singers

questions.explanation: The phrase means "Indeed, God is with the patient" (those who endure).

questions.question: Which traditional instrument is commonly used in the recitation of Arabic poetry in Northern Nigeria

options.A: Obo
options.B: Kora
options.C: Tambourine
options.D: Algaita

questions.explanation: The "Algaita" (mizmar) is a traditional reed instrument used in northern Nigerian Arabic recitation contexts.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered an element of art?

options.A: Line
options.B: Color
options.C: Texture
options.D: Perspective

questions.explanation: Perspective is a principle of design, not an element of art.

questions.question: Which principle of art is primarily used to create visual interest through differences in value, color, or texture?

options.A: Balance
options.B: Contrast
options.C: Harmony
options.D: Proportion

questions.explanation: Contrast highlights differences, making the artwork more dynamic.

questions.question: Which Nigerian artist is best known for creating the famous sculpture titled "Sculpture of a Girl"?

options.A: Ben Enwonwu
options.B: Yinka Shonibare
options.C: Dimbo Atiya
options.D: Uche Okeke

questions.explanation: Ben Enwonwu created the celebrated sculpture "Sculpture of a Girl".

questions.question: The technique of "impasto" in painting involves:

options.A: Applying thin washes of color
options.B: Using thick, heavy layers of paint
options.C: Drawing with charcoal
options.D: Mixing watercolor pigments

questions.explanation: Impasto refers to thickly applied paint that creates texture.

questions.question: In traditional Nigerian architecture, which material is most commonly used for building houses in the northern region?

options.A: Mud (Adobe)
options.B: Glass
options.C: Steel
options.D: Concrete

questions.explanation: Mud-brick or adobe construction is prevalent in northern Nigeria.

questions.question: Which of the following is primarily used to remove unwanted pigment from hair?

options.A: Bleach
options.B: Conditioner
options.C: Shampoo
options.D: Leave-in spray

questions.explanation: Bleach contains strong oxidising agents such as hydrogen peroxide and is employed specifically for colour removal.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a pre-client sanitisation routine in a cosmetology setting?

options.A: To sterilise the client’s scalp
options.B: To sanitize tools and surfaces
options.C: To apply the final treatment
options.D: To take measurements

questions.explanation: Proper disinfection of instruments and work areas prevents cross-contamination and protects both client and staff.

questions.question: In facial skincare, what does “exfoliation” refer to?

options.A: Applying moisturiser
options.B: Removing dead skin cells
options.C: Pumping serum into pores
options.D: Using a mask

questions.explanation: Exfoliation involves mechanical or chemical removal of superficial dead skin layers to improve texture and radiance.

questions.question: Which of the following actions is NOT recommended for maintaining a safe salon environment?

options.A: Cleaning mirrors daily
options.B: Wearing disposable gloves when handling chemicals
options.C: Ignoring poor ventilation
options.D: Storing hazardous chemicals out of reach of children

questions.explanation: Poor ventilation allows accumulation of vapours and dust, increasing health risks; regular cleaning and glove use are essential.

questions.question: Which organisation issues the national certificate for cosmetology qualifications in Nigeria?

options.A: National Council for Professional Hairdressers and Cosmetology (NCPHC)
options.B: West African Examinations Council
options.C: Jamaican Medical Council
options.D: International Federation of Beauty Professionals

questions.explanation: The NCPHC is the statutory body that awards the official Certificate in Cosmetology after successful completion of training and examinations.

questions.question: Which organelle is primarily responsible for producing ATP in eukaryotic cells?

options.A: Nucleus
options.B: Mitochondrion
options.C: Ribosome
options.D: Lysosome

questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration, the main source of ATP in eukaryotic cells.

questions.question: In pea plants, the allele for purple flowers (P) is dominant over white flowers (p). If a heterozygous purple-flowered plant (Pp) is crossed with a white-flowered plant (pp), what is the expected phenotypic ratio of the offspring?

options.D: All purple

questions.explanation: The cross Pp × pp yields 50% Pp (purple) and 50% pp (white), giving a 1:1 phenotypic ratio.

questions.question: Which enzyme is secreted by the pancreas to break down carbohydrates?

options.A: Amylase
options.B: Pepsin
options.C: Lipase
options.D: Trypsin

questions.explanation: Pancreatic amylase hydrolyzes starch and other polysaccharides into simpler sugars.

questions.question: In a terrestrial ecosystem, which of the following best describes the 10% rule?

options.A: Only 10% of energy is transferred from producers to primary consumers
options.B: 10% of biomass is converted to chemical energy
options.C: 10% of species are apex predators
options.D: 10% of water is lost through transpiration

questions.explanation: Approximately 10% of the energy captured by one trophic level is passed to the next level.

questions.question: Which structure produces ova in females?

options.A: Testes
options.B: Ovaries
options.C: Uterus
options.D: Fallopian tubes

questions.explanation: The ovaries contain and release the egg cells (ova) in the female reproductive system.

questions.question: Which of the following practices helps prevent cross-contamination in a catering kitchen?

options.A: Storing raw meat above vegetables
options.B: Washing hands after handling raw meat before touching ready-to-eat foods
options.C: Using the same cutting board for all foods without cleaning
options.D: Leaving food at room temperature for more than two hours

questions.explanation: Proper hand washing removes pathogens and stops bacteria from spreading to other foods.

questions.question: According to the recommended daily intake for protein for a typical adult male in Nigeria, which source provides the most bioavailable protein?

options.A: Beans and lentils
options.B: Chicken breast
options.C: Rice
options.D: Sweet potato

questions.explanation: Animal proteins such as chicken breast have higher digestibility and bioavailability compared to plant sources.

questions.question: In a commercial kitchen, what is the primary purpose of having separate hot and cold zones?

options.A: To keep staff warm during long shifts
options.B: To reduce the time needed to move ingredients between areas
options.C: To improve overall kitchen ventilation
options.D: To increase the risk of fire

questions.explanation: Separating hot and cold workflows minimizes cross-contamination and streamlines material movement.

questions.question: Which personal protective equipment (PPE) is mandatory when working with hot ovens?

options.A: Safety goggles only
options.B: Heat-resistant gloves and apron
options.C: Non-slip shoes only
options.D: No PPE required

questions.explanation: Gloves protect against thermal burns while an apron shields clothing from heat splatter.

questions.question: When labeling a prepared dish for sale, which piece of information must be included according to standard food-labeling regulations?

options.A: Name of the chef only
options.B: List of ingredients
options.C: Nutritional value per serving
options.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: Legal labels must contain the product name, ingredient list, allergen warnings, and nutritional information.

questions.question: Which element has the electron configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p³?

options.A: As
options.B: Se
options.C: Sb
options.D: Te

questions.explanation: The configuration corresponds to arsenic (As), atomic number 33. Argon (Ar) has 18 electrons; adding 3d¹⁰ (10), 4s² (2), and 4p³ (3) totals 33 electrons.

questions.question: Which element has the highest electronegativity?

options.A: F
options.B: O
options.C: N
options.D: C

questions.explanation: Fluorine (F) is the most electronegative element due to its small atomic radius and high effective nuclear charge.

questions.question: What type of bond is formed between sodium and chlorine?

options.A: Ionic
options.B: Covalent
options.C: Metallic
options.D: Hydrogen

questions.explanation: Sodium (metal) transfers an electron to chlorine (non-metal), forming an ionic bond via electrostatic attraction.

questions.question: If 10.0 g of calcium carbonate is heated, what mass of CO₂ is produced?
questions.explanation: The reaction is CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Molar mass of CaCO₃ is 100 g/mol. 10.0 g = 0.1 mol. Each mole produces 1 mole CO₂ (44 g/mol), so 0.1 × 44 = 4.4 g.

questions.question: Which of the following is a weak acid?

options.A: HCl
options.B: CH₃COOH
options.C: H₂SO₄
options.D: HNO₃

questions.explanation: CH₃COOH (acetic acid) partially dissociates in water, making it a weak acid. HCl, H₂SO₄, and HNO₃ are strong acids.

questions.question: Who was the first king of Israel?

options.A: Saul
options.B: David
options.C: Solomon
options.D: Samuel

questions.explanation: Saul was anointed by the prophet Samuel as the first king of the united monarchy of Israel (1 Samuel 10).

questions.question: Which New Testament epistle emphasizes justification by faith?

options.A: Romans
options.B: James
options.C: Hebrews
options.D: 1 Peter

questions.explanation: Paul's letter to the Romans systematically presents the doctrine of justification by faith apart from works of the law (Romans 3–5).

questions.question: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who passed by the injured man first?

options.A: Priest
options.B: Levite
options.C: Samaritan
options.D: Tax collector

questions.explanation: The priest saw the man and passed by on the other side before the Levite and the Samaritan (Luke 10:31‑32).

questions.question: The Council of Nicaea (325 AD) primarily addressed which doctrinal issue?

options.A: Nature of Christ (Arianism)
options.B: Canon of Scripture
options.C: Papal authority
options.D: Sacraments

questions.explanation: The council was convened to settle the Arian controversy, affirming that the Son is homoousios (of the same substance) with the Father.

questions.question: What is the greatest commandment according to Jesus?

options.A: Love God with all your heart
options.B: Love your neighbor as yourself
options.C: Keep the Sabbath
options.D: Do not murder

questions.explanation: Jesus cites Deuteronomy 6:5 as the first and greatest commandment, followed by the second to love one's neighbor (Matthew 22:37‑39).

questions.question: Which document is regarded as the supreme law of the Federal Republic of Nigeria?

options.A: 1979 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
options.B: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
options.C: 1978 National Assembly Decree
options.D: 1995 Military Proclamation

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution, enacted after the transition to the Fourth Republic, is the current supreme law of Nigeria.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a fundamental right in the 1999 Constitution?

options.A: Right to life
options.B: Right to education
options.C: Right to private property
options.D: Right to freedom of movement

questions.explanation: The Constitution expressly guarantees rights such as life, education and freedom of movement, but does not list private property as a fundamental right.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Executive branch of government?

options.A: Enforce laws
options.B: Make laws
options.C: Implement government policies
options.D: Conduct foreign affairs

questions.explanation: Making laws is the responsibility of the Legislature; the Executive enforces and implements laws.

questions.question: According to the 1999 Constitution, a person born in Nigeria automatically becomes a Nigerian citizen, except when:

options.A: The parents are Nigerian citizens
options.B: The parents are permanent residents
options.C: The parents have diplomatic immunity
options.D: The birth takes place in a private hospital

questions.explanation: Children born to parents with diplomatic immunity are excluded from automatic citizenship by birth under the Constitution.

questions.question: What is the minimum age required to contest for the position of President of Nigeria?

options.A: 30 years
options.B: 35 years
options.C: 40 years
options.D: 45 years

questions.explanation: Section 146 of the 1999 Constitution sets the minimum age for presidential candidates at 35 years.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines entrepreneurship in the context of Nigerian business education?

options.A: The process of identifying opportunities, taking calculated risks, and initiating new ventures.
options.B: The simple creation of goods and services for sale without any risk.
options.C: Only the financial aspect of running a business.
options.D: Routine administrative tasks performed by employees.

questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship involves spotting market gaps, assuming risk, and organizing resources to launch a business.

questions.question: What primary function of a business is concerned with meeting customer needs through research, promotion, and distribution?

options.A: Production
options.B: Marketing
options.C: Human Resource Management
options.D: Financial Accounting

questions.explanation: Marketing focuses on understanding and fulfilling customer demands via product development, promotion, and placement.

questions.question: In cost‑volume‑profit analysis, the break‑even point is reached when:

options.A: Total revenue equals total costs.
options.B: Sales volume exceeds projected demand.
options.C: Fixed costs equal total revenue.
options.D: Variable costs become zero.

questions.explanation: At break‑even, revenues cover all costs, resulting in zero profit.

questions.question: The contribution margin for a product is calculated as:

options.A: Selling price minus total fixed costs.
options.B: Selling price minus variable costs per unit.
options.C: Net profit after interest and taxes.
options.D: Operating profit divided by total assets.

questions.explanation: Contribution margin measures the profit left after subtracting variable costs per unit, showing what remains to cover fixed costs.

questions.question: Which item is NOT typically presented in a company’s cash flow statement?

options.A: Cash received from operating activities.
options.B: Cash paid for capital expenditures.
options.C: Profit from tax adjustments.
options.D: Changes in working capital accounts.

questions.explanation: The cash flow statement records cash inflows and outflows for operations, investments, and financing; it does not display accounting profit figures such as tax‑adjusted profit.

questions.question: Which component retains the BIOS configuration settings when the computer is powered off?

options.A: RAM
options.B: CMOS battery
options.C: Hard drive
options.D: Power supply

questions.explanation: The CMOS battery powers the small CMOS RAM that stores BIOS settings such as date, time, and hardware configuration when the system is off.

questions.question: In a GSM handset, which block converts baseband digital signals into radio‑frequency (RF) signals for transmission?

options.A: Baseband processor
options.B: RF transceiver
options.C: Power amplifier
options.D: Antenna

questions.explanation: The RF transceiver (often called the RF front‑end) performs digital‑to‑RF conversion, modulation, and demodulation; the power amplifier only boosts the RF signal.

questions.question: A laptop shows no sign of power. What is the first diagnostic step a technician should take?

options.A: Replace the motherboard
options.B: Test the AC adapter output voltage
options.C: Reinstall the operating system
options.D: Upgrade the RAM

questions.explanation: Verifying that the AC adapter delivers the correct voltage rules out a power‑source fault before any internal component replacement.

questions.question: What is the typical soldering‑iron tip temperature recommended for reworking surface‑mount components on a mobile‑phone PCB?
questions.explanation: A tip temperature around 350 °C provides sufficient heat for lead‑free solder on small SMD pads without damaging the board or components.

questions.question: Which identifier is permanently stored on a GSM SIM card and used by the network to authenticate the subscriber?

options.A: IMEI
options.B: IMSI
options.C: MAC address
options.D: IP address

questions.explanation: The International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) resides on the SIM and uniquely identifies the subscriber to the GSM network; the IMEI identifies the handset.

questions.question: Which component of a computer system is responsible for executing instructions?

options.A: CPU
options.B: RAM
options.C: Hard Disk
options.D: Power Supply

questions.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) performs the arithmetic and logic operations that execute program instructions.

questions.question: What is the decimal equivalent of the binary number 10110?
Which of the following is an example of application software?

options.A: Operating System
options.B: Device Driver
options.C: Word Processor
options.D: BIOS

questions.explanation: A word processor is a program that helps users create and edit documents, making it application software.

questions.question: What does the acronym URL stand for in web technology?

options.A: Uniform Resource Locator
options.B: Universal Reference Link
options.C: Unified Retrieval Language
options.D: User Request Link

questions.explanation: URL is the address used to locate resources on the Internet, standing for Uniform Resource Locator.

questions.question: In a flowchart, which symbol is used to represent a decision point?

options.A: Rectangle
options.B: Diamond
options.C: Parallelogram
options.D: Oval

questions.explanation: A diamond shape denotes a decision or branching point where a yes/no question is asked.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Central Processing Unit (CPU) in a computer?

options.A: To store data permanently
options.B: To perform calculations and execute instructions
options.C: To display output on the monitor
options.D: To input data from external devices

questions.explanation: The CPU processes instructions and performs calculations, acting as the brain of the computer.

questions.question: Convert the binary number 1101 to its decimal equivalent.
Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a relational database?

options.A: Data is stored in tables
options.B: Relationships between tables can be enforced
options.C: Data is stored in a hierarchical structure
options.D: SQL is used to query the data

questions.explanation: Relational databases use tables, not hierarchical structures; hierarchical databases are a different model.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct syntax to assign a value to a variable in Python?

options.A: myVariable = 42
options.B: myVariable 42
options.C: myVariable[42]
options.D: 42 myVariable

questions.explanation: In Python, assignment is done using the equals sign (=).

questions.question: Which of the following devices is classified as an output device?

options.A: Keyboard
options.B: Mouse
options.C: Monitor
options.D: Scanner

questions.explanation: A monitor displays information to the user, making it an output device.

questions.question: A student has two hours to either study for a mathematics test or a physics test. If she spends the two hours on mathematics, the opportunity cost is:

options.A: The time she spends studying mathematics
options.B: The grade she will obtain in physics
options.C: The next best alternative she forgone, which is studying physics
options.D: The total number of hours she studied

questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative that is given up; here it is the physics study.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best illustrates the law of demand?

options.A: When the price of rice rises, consumers buy more rice.
options.B: When the price of shoes falls, the quantity demanded increases.
options.C: When the price of a smartphone rises, the quantity demanded falls, ceteris paribus.
options.D: When the price of a book stays the same, the quantity demanded remains unchanged.

questions.explanation: The law of demand states that, all else equal, a higher price leads to a lower quantity demanded.

questions.question: If a new technology reduces the cost of production for a firm, the firm's supply curve will:

options.A: Shift leftward
options.B: Shift rightward
options.C: Remain unchanged
options.D: Become perfectly inelastic

questions.explanation: A decrease in production cost makes it cheaper to produce each quantity, so the firm is willing to supply more at each price, shifting supply right.

questions.question: The price elasticity of demand for a good is -0.5. This indicates that demand is:

options.A: Elastic
options.B: Inelastic
options.C: Perfectly elastic
options.D: Perfectly inelastic

questions.explanation: An elasticity between 0 and -1 means demand is inelastic; quantity demanded changes less than proportionally to price.

questions.question: Which indicator is most commonly used to measure inflation in a country?

options.A: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
options.B: Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
options.C: Unemployment rate
options.D: Balance of trade

questions.explanation: The CPI tracks the average change in prices of a basket of consumer goods and services, providing the standard measure of inflation.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect tense?

options.A: She has never visited Lagos before.
options.B: She visited Lagos last year.
options.C: She will have visited Lagos by next week.
options.D: She visits Lagos every weekend.

questions.explanation: Present perfect indicates experience up to the present moment without a specific time frame.

questions.question: The word 'resilient' most closely means:

options.A: fragile
options.B: adaptable
options.C: optimistic
options.D: silent

questions.explanation: Resilient describes the ability to recover quickly from difficulties.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'Her performance was a ____ of effort.'

options.A: miracle
options.B: disaster
options.C: obstacle
options.D: challenge

questions.explanation: Miracle conveys an unexpected success resulting from great effort.

questions.question: Select the correctly punctuated version of the following sentence:

options.A: When I reached the library, I realized that my textbook was missing.
options.B: When I reached the library, I realized, that my textbook was missing.
options.C: When I reached the library, I realized that, my textbook was missing.
options.D: When I reached the library, I realized that my textbook was missing, because it was lost.

questions.explanation: Only one comma after the introductory dependent clause is required.

questions.question: Based on the passage, which statement can be inferred about Tobio's study routine?

options.A: He studies only once a week.
options.B: He relies solely on textbooks.
options.C: He engages in collaborative learning.
options.D: He avoids any form of revision.

questions.explanation: Forming a study circle demonstrates participation in group study.

questions.question: When taking body measurements for a basic bodice, which measurement is taken around the fullest part of the chest?

options.A: Chest
options.B: Waist
options.C: Hip
options.D: Shoulder

questions.explanation: The chest (bust) measurement is taken at the fullest part of the chest to ensure proper fit of the bodice.

questions.question: Which type of stitch is commonly used for temporary basting of fabric pieces before permanent sewing?

options.A: Backstitch
options.B: Running stitch
options.C: Chain stitch
options.D: Overlock stitch

questions.explanation: Running stitch creates long, loose stitches that can be easily removed, making it ideal for basting.

questions.question: Which fabric is most suitable for a lightweight summer dress because of its breathability?

options.A: Wool
options.B: Cotton
options.C: Polyester
options.D: Silk

questions.explanation: Cotton is a natural fibre that allows air circulation, making it comfortable for summer garments.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a seam allowance in garment construction?

options.A: To add decorative stitching
options.B: To prevent fabric fraying
options.C: To allow for sewing and fitting adjustments
options.D: To reduce the weight of the garment

questions.explanation: Seam allowance provides extra fabric for stitching and ensures the finished garment fits correctly.

questions.question: After sewing a garment, which is the recommended order for pressing the seams?

options.A: Press the entire garment first, then press individual seams
options.B: Press individual seams first, then press the whole garment
options.C: Press only with steam, no dry iron
options.D: Press with the iron set to dry heat only

questions.explanation: Pressing seams first sets the stitch line, and then pressing the whole garment smooths the final shape.

questions.question: Which nutrient is primarily responsible for building and repairing body tissues?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Proteins
options.C: Fats
options.D: Vitamins

questions.explanation: Proteins provide amino acids that are used for tissue growth and repair.

questions.question: A deficiency of which vitamin leads to night blindness?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Vitamin D
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Vitamin K

questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed for the synthesis of rhodopsin in the retina; its deficiency causes night blindness.

questions.question: Which of the following food preservation methods works by reducing water activity?

options.A: Pasteurization
options.B: Freezing
options.C: Salting
options.D: Irradiation

questions.explanation: Salting draws moisture out of food, lowering water activity and inhibiting microbial growth.

questions.question: In the Nigerian food guide pyramid, which group forms the base (largest portion) of a healthy diet?

options.A: Fruits and vegetables
options.B: Cereals, grains and tubers
options.C: Proteins (meat, fish, legumes)
options.D: Fats and oils

questions.explanation: Cereals, grains and tubers supply the majority of energy and should be consumed in the largest amounts.

questions.question: Which condition is characterized by edema, irritability, and hair changes due to severe protein deficiency in children?

options.A: Kwashiorkor
options.B: Marasmus
